---
title: "Explore a 2D convolution"
toc: false
page-layout: full
---

A two-dimensional convolution applies one small matrix of weights at every
valid image location. This explorer uses a grayscale Columbia Engineering logo:
choose a 3 × 3 kernel, then watch its output image appear as the
kernel scans across the original.

::: {.callout-tip}
## What to watch

The red square marks the current 3 × 3 image patch. Its nine pixel
values are multiplied by the nine kernel weights, summed, and written to the
highlighted location in the filtered image.
:::

```{=html}
<div id="convolution-2d-explorer" class="convolution-2d-explorer" aria-label="Interactive two-dimensional convolution explorer">
  <div class="convolution-2d-controls">
    <div>
      <span class="convolution-eyebrow">Choose a 3 × 3 kernel</span>
      <p id="convolution-2d-description">A local mean filter smooths small visual variations.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="convolution-2d-filter-buttons" role="group" aria-label="Choose a two-dimensional convolution kernel">
      <button type="button" class="convolution-2d-filter is-active" data-filter="blur">Blur</button>
      <button type="button" class="convolution-2d-filter" data-filter="vertical">Vertical edges</button>
      <button type="button" class="convolution-2d-filter" data-filter="horizontal">Horizontal edges</button>
      <button type="button" class="convolution-2d-filter" data-filter="sharpen">Sharpen</button>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="convolution-2d-toolbar clt-buttons">
    <button id="convolution-2d-play" type="button" class="regression-sampling-primary">Play all</button>
    <button id="convolution-2d-reset" type="button">Reset</button>
    <output id="convolution-2d-status" class="convolution-status" aria-live="polite"></output>
  </div>

  <div class="convolution-2d-workbench">
    <section class="convolution-2d-panel convolution-2d-images" aria-labelledby="convolution-2d-images-heading">
      <div class="convolution-panel-heading">
        <h2 id="convolution-2d-images-heading">A kernel slides over the image</h2>
        <p>The filtered image starts blank, then receives one output pixel for each valid 3 × 3 window.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="convolution-2d-image-grid">
        <figure>
          <figcaption>Original grayscale image</figcaption>
          <canvas id="convolution-2d-source" width="336" height="336" aria-label="Original grayscale Columbia Engineering logo with an active three-by-three patch"></canvas>
        </figure>
        <figure>
          <figcaption>Filtered image</figcaption>
          <canvas id="convolution-2d-output" width="336" height="336" aria-label="Filtered output image with the current output pixel highlighted"></canvas>
        </figure>
      </div>
    </section>

    <aside class="convolution-2d-panel convolution-2d-kernel-panel" aria-labelledby="convolution-2d-kernel-heading">
      <div class="convolution-panel-heading">
        <h2 id="convolution-2d-kernel-heading">Current kernel</h2>
        <p>The same nine weights are reused at every image location.</p>
      </div>
      <div id="convolution-2d-kernel-grid" class="convolution-2d-kernel-grid" aria-live="polite"></div>
      <p id="convolution-2d-formula" class="convolution-2d-formula"></p>
    </aside>
  </div>
</div>
```

For the two edge filters, the displayed image shows the *magnitude* of the
signed convolution response, so both dark-to-light and light-to-dark edges are
visible. The image is the [Columbia Engineering logo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Columbia_Engineering_logo.svg), rendered here in grayscale.
